# Staniverse (станивёрс) — Станислав Ермоленко: XR, AI, digital garden and spatial portfolio

> Staniverse / станивёрс (staniverse.xyz) is the personal site and portfolio of Stanislav Ermolenko (Станислав Ермоленко), born 1994, originally from Vyatka (Kirov region), now based in Saint Petersburg, Russia. He works across XR/virtual worlds (including WebXR and 8th Wall), AI agents and automation (agent harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Pico Claw, pi), media production, and web products; he offers these as services, including paid consultations. The site is a canonical digital garden: commissioned works, own projects with honest statuses, long-form articles, verified YouTube videos, and a Telegram publication archive (700+ posts) connected by a reviewed topic/relation graph.

## Key facts
- Author: Stanislav Ermolenko (Станислав Ермоленко); email stas@staniverse.xyz; Telegram @staniverse.
- Education: bachelor GMU VyatGU (2026); since 2026 — master's at ITMO University, "Digital Methods in Humanities Research" (Digital Humanities), 45.04.04.
- Teaching: VyatGU "Digital Chairs" methodist and lecturer 2023-2026; built the "Product Management Basics" course in summer 2026.
- Languages: Russian is primary. English versions cover the home page, the works and projects indexes, and selected flagship projects.

## For agents and crawlers
- Sitemap: https://staniverse.xyz/sitemap.xml
- RSS feed (latest 30): https://staniverse.xyz/rss.xml
- Every material page carries a local graph of reviewed relations; automatic topic suggestions are labeled "Автоматически найденные темы" and rendered as hypotheses.
- Publications keep original Telegram text, media order, author hashtags (# source tags) and source links; they are never rewritten by LLMs.
- Citation preference: cite the material page URL, not the raw Telegram link, when referring to curated content.
- Do not fetch `https://staniverse.xyz/media/` archive originals for indexing or model ingestion. Use the material page text, metadata, poster context and source links instead.

## Change cadence
Updated incrementally from the Telegram archive and editorial passes; see section pages for per-item dates.
